name: SAN MARINO

flag.title: San Marino
flag.note: White over sky-blue, coat of arms centred

lead: Perched on a rocky mountain surrounded by Italy, San Marino is the world's oldest republic. Three medieval towers crown its peak like a stone crown. Founded in AD 301 by a stonemason named Marinus, it has never been conquered — and its people celebrate that every year with crossbow tournaments and fireworks around the ancient walls.

sections.geography: A mountain kingdom in the sky

geo: San Marino sits atop Monte Titano, a limestone mountain rising 749 m above the Italian plains. The whole country covers just 61 km² — you could walk across it in a morning. Three ancient towers crown the three peaks, with views stretching to the Adriatic on clear days.

The land rolls from rocky ridges down through oak and chestnut woods into green valleys. Because the mountain catches clouds, San Marino is cooler and rainier than the plains below, which keeps the forests lush and the air wonderfully fresh year round.
animals: Monte Titano's limestone cliffs are home to peregrine falcons — San Marino's national bird and the fastest animal on Earth, diving at over 300 km/h to catch birds in mid-air. Watching one stoop from the tower ramparts feels like seeing a feathered thunderbolt.

The oak woods shelter red foxes, badgers, hedgehogs and martens. Roe deer browse the quieter valleys while buzzards wheel overhead. Because the country is small and people protect the land carefully, wildlife thrives close to the medieval city walls.
culture: San Marino's most famous sweet is the Torta Tre Monti — wafer layers sandwiched with hazelnut and cocoa cream, shaped like the three towers. Local piadina flatbread is stuffed with prosciutto or stracchino cheese and eaten folded like a warm hug.

Every 3 September — national day — a Grand Crossbow Competition fills the ancient stone quarry below the walls. Teams from the nine castelli duel in medieval costume, and fireworks burst around the illuminated towers. In March, bonfires called focheracce light up every castle district to celebrate fathers and spring.
history: A stonemason named Marinus sailed from the island of Rab to escape Roman persecution. Around AD 301, he climbed Monte Titano, built a chapel, and declared the land free. His last words: 'I leave you free from both men' — the Emperor and the Pope.

Over 17 centuries San Marino survived wars and Napoleon (who offered to enlarge it; they declined). It abolished the death penalty in 1865, one of the world's first. Surrounded by Italy, it has kept full independence ever since.
wows: San Marino is the world's oldest republic, founded in AD 301 — over 1,700 years ago.
The whole country is smaller than the city of Florence, yet has its own army and stamps.
San Marino has TWO heads of state at once, called Captains Regent, who swap out every six months.
It was among the first countries ever to abolish the death penalty, in 1865.
San Marino's football team scored after just 8.3 seconds vs England — fastest international goal ever.
Despite its tiny size, San Marino is one of Europe's most prosperous countries by income per person.
Collectors worldwide buy San Marino stamps just to own them — stamp sales fund a slice of the budget.

myths.myth: San Marino is part of Italy
myths.fact: It is surrounded by Italy but is a fully independent republic with its own government, passport, and laws since AD 301.
San Marino holds a United Nations seat, competes at the Olympics, and ranks among the world's top 15 nations by income per person.
